Meanwhile I am fighting my insurance company who I pay $300 every month (even though I have insurance through my work who pays 75% of premiums) to actually pay their portion to help defray the costs of my ongoing medical problems, which I often end up paying for out of pocket.

I am paying $110 per appointment out of pocket to see my physical therapist for the past 3 months because my insurance company is like "Lol, bro aren't you better yet? You saw them like 6 times, that should be enough so no more money for you."

For anyone who actually needs medical care, it is the fucking deal of a lifetime to only have to pay a bit extra in taxes rather than go through this.

Alright you Canuks... what do you Get for your taxes?

Socialized health care (no matter what you think, I understand it can take a long time to be seen). Retirement benefits? I know that one or more of the Scandinavian countries has a very well funded "retirement" fund. Anything else?

Lay down some education...

For reference, I pay 10% for housing (mortgage, insurance, property taxes ~ but that goes to 16% if you include utilities), 5% on food and probably closer to 1% on clothing.... helps being old and no giving a damn about fashion, I happily wear 5 year old shirts that only cost me ~$20 to buy. But my health insurance (the cheapest high deductible plan I can find) takes 8% and I STILL have to pay $8,000 out of pocket before insurance covers anything (bringing things to just shy of 20%). No retirement benefits in the US to speak of, certainly nothing you can live on and that's if it's even still alive and kicking in 25 years when I come of age. With income tax in the 20% range, we're spending 28~40% depending on if we need medical care (infrequent, thankfully). And we are Damn close to 40% if we opted to buy 'all inclusive' medical coverage... which means we are right in line with Canada.
